newsitem.title: ZAIRE: More than 14 people massacred in Zairean village.
newsitem.headline: More than 14 people massacred in Zairean village.

text.p: More than 14 bodies lay in the eastern Zairean village of Bumba on Monday from a massacre by attackers identified by refugees who escaped to Rwanda as Tutsi rebels.
As a Reuters Television cameraman I visited Bumba with Zairean volunteers who entered Zaire from Rwanda for Medecins sans Frontieres (Doctors Without Borders) to try to evacuate any wounded.
The first house in Bumba as we approached on foot from the border was razed to the ground with corrugated iron lying on a pile of at least six badly burned bodies tied together.
A human rib cage poked out from the pile of corpses in the middle of the small house, which was still smouldering.

Bumba and the neighbouring Rwandan refugee camp of Kibumba were first attacked on Friday. The 200,000 residents of Kibumba fled on Saturday but much of the bloodshed in Bumba appeared Deeper into the village below a chief's home, the foot of an adult and the arm of a small child poked out of the earth in an onion patch. A dog was carrying a leg from a small child in its mouth.
The child lay nearby, its face eaten away, apparently by the dog.
As I stood in the onion patch, I felt the ground move under my feet as if others were buried there and soil was settling.
Further into the village a Zairean volunteer among the group of 20 uncovered a pit latrine covered with logs and grass.
The first corpse he saw was his brother-in-law with his arms tied behind his back. Three other bodies were in the latrine.
In another house, the body of an elderly man lay still huddled in the fetal position in the corner of his kitchen.
Residents who had fled said that when shooting started on Friday people went to the chief's house for shelter but everyone who had gone there had been massacred by unidentified gunmen.
Before we could visit the chief's house, shooting suddenly started in the distance. Suddenly the bullets were very close.
After about 20 to 30 minutes of firing, we escaped back to Rwanda. No bodies or wounded were brought out of Bumba by us.
"The Banyamulenge are animals, they will eat your hearts out," said a Rwandan soldier. "Whoever like you goes down into Bumba must be mad. Even we soldiers don't dare to go there."

Zairean refugees, speaking to a Reuters correspondent while Rwandan soldiers listened at the crossing, identified the attackers as Tutsi rebels. Zaire has accused Rwandan troops of invading the east, a charge denied by Rwanda's government.
At the Mutura crossing point in Rwanda, MSF doctors were treating a small girl aged about four carried out of Bumba earlier with a deep bullet wound to one of her shoulders.
Relatives said she was found in a pile of corpses in a house and she and her sister were the only survivors from her family.
